elements.title: Violet Wong (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that ten-year-old Violet Wong (pictured) received a gold watch after performing for General Chiang Kai-shek?

elements.title: the second (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Alabama and Clemson played each other in the championship game of the second and third College Football Playoffs?

elements.title: Jindřich Marco (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that an irreverent photograph of Czechoslovak president Klement Gottwald brought a ten-year sentence for the photojournalist Jindřich Marco, who had to serve seven years in uranium mines?

elements.title: a cathedral (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that despite having built a cathedral, Bishop Joseph Crétin said that his diocese did not have one?

elements.title: Jerónimo Muñoz (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Jerónimo Muñoz's mastery of Hebrew purportedly caused Jews to assert that Muñoz was himself a Jew?

elements.title: an Oregon radio station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that an Oregon radio station stayed on the air through a major windstorm even though a tree fell into its studios?

elements.title: Lee Ek Tieng (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Lee Kuan Yew stated that "there would have been no clean and green Singapore without Lee Ek Tieng"?

elements.title: A Voyage to the Moon (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the 1827 novel A Voyage to the Moon contains the first use of anti-gravity for space travel in science fiction?

elements.title: Eurovision Song Contest 1985 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a wardrobe malfunction at the Eurovision Song Contest 1985 was staged because the host wanted the audience "to wake up a little"?
